product.name: Meiji SAVAS Milk Protein
product.audience: Gym users, office workers managing weight, convenience-store breakfast buyers, light-fitness women, and college students who want easy daily protein intake
product.priceRange: Premium imported RTD protein drink; expected RMB 12-20 per bottle depending on channel
product.positioning: A Japanese ready-to-drink protein beverage for daily protein convenience, not a bodybuilding-only supplement or aggressive meal-replacement product
sellingPoints: Fits breakfast, office snack, post-workout, and convenience-store routines

trend.name: High-protein snacking / light fitness / convenience-store healthy breakfast
trend.region: China, with Japan as product-format benchmark
trend.description: Protein is moving from gym supplement behavior into lighter daily routines: breakfast backup, office snack, post-workout drink, and weight-management swap for sugary drinks or heavy snacks.
trend.drivenBy: Light-fitness creators, weight-management content, convenience-store product discovery, and Japanese RTD protein benchmarks
trend.format: Convenience-store protein find, what I drink after a light workout, high-protein breakfast in a rush, office snack swap, daily protein without powder
trend.whyPopular: Consumers want convenient health routines without mixing powder, cooking, or adopting an intense bodybuilding identity.
trend.exampleContent: A creator compares a normal sweet bottled drink, a protein powder shaker, and a SAVAS-style chilled protein drink for a workday breakfast or post-gym convenience-store stop.
trend.controversy: Protein and weight-management messaging can drift into diet anxiety, meal-replacement overclaiming, or pseudo-scientific health claims.
